mainTopic: Davening behind one's רב; davening early on ערב שבת and מוצאי שבת; whether עַרְבִית is רשות or חובה, and the removal of רבן גמליאל as נשיא.
overview: The amud opens by asking how רבי ירמיה בר אבא could daven behind רב, since a student may not pray next to or behind his teacher. A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר makes this worse: it says such disrespect drives the שכינה away from ישראל. The גמרא answers that he was a תלמיד חבר, a student who was also a colleague. Next the גמרא discusses davening the שבת prayer early. Someone who does so on purpose must stop working, but a prayer said by mistake does not bind an individual, though a צבור's mistaken prayer stands. שמואל rules that one may daven שבת early and make קידוש, and daven מוצאי שבת early and make הבדלה. Then the גמרא explains the משנה's words 'תפלת הערב אין לה קבע' as meaning that עַרְבִית is רשות, the view of רבי יהושע against רבן גמליאל. A famous story follows: רבן גמליאל publicly embarrasses רבי יהושע over this question, the people remove רבן גמליאל as נשיא, and they choose רבי אלעזר בן עזריה to replace him. The amud ends as he consults his wife, and her answer comes on the next amud.

steps.title: A student may not pray next to or behind his teacher
steps.stepSummary: The end of the rule the גמרא is using to challenge רבי ירמיה בר אבא: a person should not pray next to his רב or behind his רב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A person should not pray next to his teacher, and not behind his teacher.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes quoting a rule it is using to challenge רבי ירמיה בר אבא, who davened behind רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule names two places a student may not stand while davening, next to his teacher and behind him. Because רבי ירמיה בר אבא davened behind רב, he seems to have broken this rule.

phrases.english: not next to his teacher,
phrases.notes: This finishes a rule from the previous amud about places where a person should never pray.

phrases.english: and not behind his teacher.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא כְּנֶגֶד רַבּוֹ, וְלֹא אֲחוֹרֵי רַבּוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the challenge that began just before this text.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא davening behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A rule forbids praying behind one's teacher, so his conduct seems forbidden.

steps.title: רבי אליעזר: disrespecting a teacher drives away the שכינה
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא of רבי אליעזר lists five ways of disrespecting a teacher, including praying behind him, and says they cause the שכינה to leave ישראל.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in a ברייתא that רבי אליעזר says: Someone who prays behind his teacher, greets his teacher, returns his teacher's greeting, sets up a rival yeshiva to his teacher's, or says something he did not hear from his teacher, causes the שכינה to leave ישראל.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that makes the challenge even stronger. Praying behind one's teacher is not just improper, it is serious enough to drive away the שכינה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 1 only said a student should not pray behind his teacher. This ברייתא puts the act on a list of serious failures of respect with a very harsh result. That makes it even harder to explain how רבי ירמיה בר אבא could do it.

keyTerms.meaning: it was taught in a ברייתא
one who sets up a rival yeshiva

phrases.english: And it was taught: Rabbi Eliezer says:
One who prays behind his teacher,
and one who greets his teacher,
phrases.notes: He means greeting the teacher the way you would greet an equal.

phrases.english: and one who returns his teacher's greeting,
and one who sets himself against his teacher's yeshiva,

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאוֹמֵר דָּבָר שֶׁלֹּא שָׁמַע מִפִּי רַבּוֹ —
phrases.english: and one who says something he did not hear from his teacher's mouth,
causes the Divine Presence to withdraw from Israel!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Makes the challenge in step 1 stronger with an earlier source.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי ירמיה בר אבא davening behind רב.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If praying behind one's teacher drives away the שכינה, a great חכם surely would not do it.

steps.title: רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a student and a colleague
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר, so the rules for an ordinary student did not apply to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי ירמיה בר אבא is different, because he was a student who was also a colleague.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. רבי ירמיה בר אבא was not an ordinary student of רב, he was close to being his equal.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rules in steps 1 and 2 are about an ordinary student and his teacher. A תלמיד חבר is partly a peer, so he may stand behind his teacher without it being disrespectful.

keyTerms.meaning: a student who is also a colleague

phrases.english: Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba is different,
since he was a student-colleague.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of steps 1 and 2.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the rule. It applies to an ordinary student and not to a תלמיד חבר.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי ירמיה בר אבא was an ordinary student who broke the rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: As a תלמיד חבר he was allowed to pray behind רב.
steps.whatToRemember: The rules about not praying behind one's teacher are for an ordinary student. A תלמיד חבר is an exception.

steps.title: Proof: he spoke to רב as an equal
steps.stepSummary: Support for the answer: רבי ירמיה בר אבא asked רב 'Did you stop working?' in the 'you' form, instead of the respectful 'Did the master stop?'
steps.simpleTranslation: That is why רבי ירמיה בר אבא said to רב: Did you separate yourself from work? רב answered: Yes, I separated myself. He did not say 'Did the master separate himself?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings support that רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר. He spoke to רב the way a colleague speaks, not the way a student speaks.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A plain student would speak to his teacher in the third person, 'the master'. רבי ירמיה בר אבא said 'you', and רב answered him without objecting. This shows their relationship was close to equal.

keyTerms.meaning: and that is why, and this explains
master, a respectful way to address a teacher

phrases.english: And this is why he said to him,
Rabbi Yirmeya bar Abba to Rav:
Did you separate yourself?
phrases.notes: He's asking whether רב, who had davened the שבת prayer early, had already stopped doing work.

phrases.english: He said to him: Yes, I separated myself.
And he did not say, 'Did the master separate himself?'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer in step 3.
steps.raayaObject: That רבי ירמיה בר אבא was a תלמיד חבר of רב.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The way he spoke to רב, saying 'you' instead of 'the master'.

steps.title: Did רב really have to stop working?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether someone who davened the שבת prayer early must stop working. רבי davened שבת early and then still went to the bathhouse.
steps.simpleTranslation: Did he really need to separate himself? But רבי אבין said: Once רבי davened the שבת prayer on ערב שבת, went into the bathhouse, came out, and taught us our chapters, and it was not yet dark!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at רב's answer, 'I stopped working', and asks whether stopping was even required.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If davening the שבת prayer early made it שבת for that person, he could not go to the bathhouse afterward. Yet רבי did exactly that before dark. This suggests that davening early does not require stopping work.

keyTerms.meaning: and did he really separate himself?

phrases.english: And did he really separate himself?
But didn't Rabbi Avin say:
Once Rabbi prayed
phrases.notes: 'רבי' with no name is רבי יהודה הנשיא.

phrases.english: the Shabbat prayer on Shabbat eve,
and he went into the bathhouse, and came out,
and taught us our chapters,
and it was still not dark!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up a detail from the story in step 4 and opens a new question.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב's statement that he stopped working after davening the שבת prayer early.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי went to the bathhouse after davening שבת early, which shows that stopping work is not required.

steps.title: רבא: he only went in to sweat, before the גזירה
steps.stepSummary: רבא answers that רבי went into the bathhouse only to sweat, and that this was before the חכמים made their גזירה against it.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: That was a case where he went in to sweat, and it was before the decree.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the challenge. What רבי did was not real work and was still allowed at that time, so the story does not prove anything.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Sweating in a bathhouse is not a forbidden מלאכה. It only became forbidden on שבת later, through a גזירה of the חכמים. So רבי could do it even after accepting שבת, and there is still a requirement to stop actual work.

phrases.english: Rava said:
That was where he went in to sweat,
and it was before the decree.
phrases.notes: This is the decree that later banned sweating in a bathhouse on שבת.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 5.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the case. The bathhouse visit was only for sweating, which was allowed at that time.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We thought רבי did a forbidden activity after accepting שבת early.
steps.terutzMaskana: Sweating was permitted before the גזירה, so a person who accepts שבת early must still stop real work.
steps.whatToRemember: Someone who davens the שבת prayer early does stop working. The story about רבי does not contradict this, because he only went in to sweat, before the גזירה.

steps.title: אביי let רב דימי work after davening
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the idea that someone who davened the שבת prayer early may not work, because אביי let רב דימי בר ליואי fumigate baskets.
steps.simpleTranslation: Is that really so? But אביי allowed רב דימי בר ליואי to fumigate baskets with sulfur!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the assumption from the last steps, that once you daven the שבת prayer early you must stop working. It brings a case where אביי allowed work after that davening.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Steps 5-6 assumed that davening שבת early makes it שבת for you, so you must stop doing מלאכה. Here רב דימי בר ליואי had davened, yet אביי let him do real work. That suggests the early davening does not bind a person at all.

keyTerms.meaning: to smoke baskets with sulfur (a kind of work)

phrases.english: Is that so? But didn't Abaye permit
Rav Dimi bar Liva'ei
to fumigate baskets with sulfur!
phrases.notes: The גמרא takes for granted that רב דימי had already davened the שבת prayer when this happened.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the assumption behind steps 5-6 that an early שבת prayer forbids work.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that one who davened שבת early must stop doing מלאכה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: אביי allowed real work after the early שבת prayer, so that prayer seems not to bind.

steps.title: That davening was a mistake
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that רב דימי's davening was a טעות, so it did not make שבת start for him.
steps.simpleTranslation: That was a mistake.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב דימי did not choose to start שבת early. He davened by mistake, so his davening did not bind him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about stopping work applies when someone means to take on שבת early. A prayer said by טעות is not a real acceptance of שבת, so אביי could let him work. The rule from before stays in place.

phrases.english: That was a mistake.
phrases.notes: He thought it was already dark when he davened, so he never really meant to start שבת early.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 7 by redefining רב דימי's case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a mistaken prayer versus a deliberate early acceptance.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: אביי's permission shows that early davening never forbids work.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a deliberate early שבת prayer binds. A mistaken one does not.

steps.title: Can a mistaken prayer be undone? רבי's ruling says no
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether a טעות can be undone. It brings אבידן's story: people davened מוצאי שבת on שבת by mistake, and רבי said their davening still counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: But can a mistake be undone? Didn't אבידן say: Once the sky was covered with clouds, and the people thought it was already night. They went into the shul and davened the מוצאי שבת prayer while it was still שבת. Then the clouds scattered and the sun came out. They came and asked רבי, and he said: Since they davened, they davened!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer of step 8. It shows a case where a prayer said by mistake was NOT undone; it still counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In אבידן's story the people davened מוצאי שבת too early by טעות, and רבי ruled that the davening stands. If a mistaken prayer stays valid, then רב דימי's mistaken שבת prayer should also stand, and he should not have been allowed to work. So 'it was a mistake' seems not to be a good answer.
steps.confusionAlert: רבי's words 'since they davened, they davened' do not mean they may do weekday work while it is still day. They mean only that the prayer they said counts and does not need to be said again.

phrases.english: But can a mistake be undone?
But didn't Avidan say:
Once the sky became covered with clouds,
and the people thought it was already dark,
they went into the shul
and davened the prayer of the end of Shabbat while it was still Shabbat.
Then the clouds scattered and the sun shone,
and they came and asked Rabbi.
He said: Since they davened, they davened!
phrases.notes: In other words, their prayer counts and they don't have to daven it again.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְטָעוּתָא מִי הָדְרָא? וְהָא אָמַר אֲבִידָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 8 that a mistaken prayer does not count.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that רב דימי's prayer did not bind him because it was a טעות.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי ruled that a prayer said by mistake still stands, so a mistake does not cancel a prayer.

steps.title: A community is different
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that a צבור is different: we do not trouble a whole community to daven again, so their mistaken prayer stands. An individual's mistaken prayer does not.
steps.simpleTranslation: A community is different, because we do not trouble them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends step 8 by showing that רבי's ruling was a special rule for a צבור.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי let the prayer stand only because it is too much trouble to gather a whole community to daven again. An individual like רב דימי is not given that special treatment, so his mistaken prayer does not count, and it does not bind him to stop working.
steps.whatToRemember: An individual who davens שבת early by mistake is not bound by it and may still work. A צבור's mistaken prayer stands, because we do not burden the community to daven again.

phrases.english: A community is different,
because we do not trouble them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 9 and so keeps the answer of step 8 in place.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishing the case: a community versus an individual.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי's ruling shows that any mistaken prayer stands.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a צבור's mistaken prayer stands, so as not to burden them. An individual's mistaken prayer does not.

steps.title: Two אמוראים who davened at the edges of שבת
steps.stepSummary: רבי חייא בר אבין reports that רב davened the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת, and רבי יאשיה davened the מוצאי שבת תפילה while it was still שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי חייא בר אבין said: רב would daven the שבת prayer on Friday before nightfall. רבי יאשיה would daven the מוצאי שבת prayer while it was still שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a report about two great people who davened early: one at the start of שבת and one at the end. This sets up the two questions that come next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This continues the topic of davening a תפילה before its normal time. Now we have real examples on both edges of שבת. The next steps ask what else these people may do after davening early.

phrases.english: Rabbi Chiyya bar Avin said:

phrases.aramaic: רַב צַלִּי שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת,
phrases.english: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on the eve of Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת.
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya would pray the prayer of the conclusion of Shabbat on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the debate about mistaken early prayer to reports of planned early davening on both ends of שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רב davened the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת; רבי יאשיה davened the מוצאי שבת תפילה on שבת.

steps.title: After davening שבת early, may one say קידוש?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רב, having davened the שבת תפילה on Friday afternoon, would also say קידוש over a cup then.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב davened the שבת prayer on Friday before nightfall, did he also say קידוש over a cup of wine, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a real question about רב's practice: after davening שבת early, may he also make קידוש early?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Davening early shows that the person accepted שבת. The question is whether קידוש, the blessing of שבת over wine, can also be said before nightfall, or whether it must wait until it is really night.

keyTerms.meaning: Here it means קידוש, the blessing that sanctifies שבת

phrases.aramaic: רַב צַלִּי שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת:
phrases.english: Rav prayed the Shabbat prayer on the eve of Shabbat:
Does he recite kiddush over the cup,

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר קְדוּשָּׁה עַל הַכּוֹס?
phrases.english: or does he not recite kiddush over the cup?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר קְדוּשָּׁה עַל הַכּוֹס, אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר קְדוּשָּׁה עַל הַכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the first case reported in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether קידוש over a cup may be said right after davening the שבת תפילה early, before nightfall.

steps.title: שמואל: yes, one may say קידוש early, and the הלכה follows him
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן quotes שמואל that one may daven the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת and say קידוש over a cup. The הלכה follows שמואל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב נחמן said in the name of שמואל: A person may daven the שבת prayer on Friday before nightfall and say קידוש over a cup. And the הלכה follows him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ruling from שמואל: yes, after davening early you may also make קידוש early. Then it adds that this is the final הלכה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once a person has brought in שבת early by davening, קידוש can follow right away, even though it is still day. The words 'והלכתא כוותיה' make this the practical ruling.

keyTerms.meaning: 'Come and hear', introducing a source that answers the question
'And the הלכה is like him', the final practical ruling

steps.whatToRemember: One who davens the שבת תפילה early on ערב שבת may also say קידוש early, and this is the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ruling is the basis for bringing in שבת early on Friday and making קידוש before dark.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Nachman said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת
phrases.english: A person may pray the Shabbat prayer on the eve of Shabbat
and recite kiddush over the cup.
And the halakha is in accordance with him.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב נַחְמָן אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קידוש question of step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. One may daven the שבת תפילה early and say קידוש over a cup, and the הלכה follows שמואל.

steps.title: After davening מוצאי שבת early, may one say הבדלה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether רבי יאשיה, who davened the מוצאי שבת תפילה while it was still שבת, would also say הבדלה over a cup then.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יאשיה davened the מוצאי שבת prayer while it was still שבת, did he also say הבדלה over a cup, or not?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא asks the same kind of question about the second case: after davening מוצאי שבת early, may one also make הבדלה early?
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 12 at the other end of שבת. קידוש marks the start of שבת, and הבדלה marks its end. The question is whether הבדלה may be said while it is still daytime on שבת.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing that separates שבת from the weekday

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה מְצַלֵּי שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yoshiya would pray the prayer of the conclusion of Shabbat on Shabbat:
does he recite havdala over the cup

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס?
phrases.english: or does he not recite havdala over the cup?

steps.triggerLanguage: אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס אוֹ אֵינוֹ אוֹמֵר הַבְדָּלָה עַל הַכּוֹס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Parallel question about the second case reported in step 11.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether הבדלה over a cup may be said right after davening the מוצאי שבת תפילה while it is still שבת.

steps.title: שמואל: yes, one may say הבדלה early
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל that one may daven the מוצאי שבת תפילה on שבת and say הבדלה over a cup.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: רב יהודה said in the name of שמואל: A person may daven the מוצאי שבת prayer while it is still שבת and say הבדלה over a cup.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with another ruling from שמואל: yes, after davening מוצאי שבת early you may also make הבדלה early.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two answers match. Just as קידוש may follow an early שבת תפילה, הבדלה may follow an early מוצאי שבת תפילה. Unlike step 13, the גמרא does not add 'והלכתא כוותיה' here.

keyTerms.meaning: The אמורא who reports this ruling from שמואל

steps.whatToRemember: שמואל allows both: קידוש after an early שבת תפילה, and הבדלה after an early מוצאי שבת תפילה.

phrases.english: Come and hear,
as Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:

phrases.aramaic: מִתְפַּלֵּל אָדָם שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת
phrases.english: A person may pray the prayer of the conclusion of Shabbat on Shabbat
and recite havdala over the cup.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע דְּאָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the הבדלה question of step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. One may daven the מוצאי שבת תפילה on שבת and say הבדלה over a cup.

steps.title: A story: a תנא davened שבת early beside a pillar
steps.stepSummary: Through a long chain of teachers, רב reports that beside a certain pillar, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי davened the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבי אסי, in the name of רבי אלעזר, in the name of רבי חנינא, in the name of רב: Beside this pillar, רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי davened the שבת prayer on Friday before nightfall.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a story showing that a great תנא davened the שבת תפילה early. This is one version of the story, and the next step gives another version.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds an earlier example, from a תנא, of davening שבת early, which supports the practice from steps 11 to 13. The long chain of names shows how carefully the story was passed down.

keyTerms.meaning: A תנא, the son of רבי יוסי

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabbi Asi said

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב:
phrases.english: that Rabbi Elazar said that Rabbi Chanina said that Rav said:
Beside this pillar
Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei, prayed
the Shabbat prayer on the eve of Shabbat.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבִּי אַסִּי אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר אָמַר רַבִּי חֲנִינָא אָמַר רַב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a story about a תנא who davened the שבת תפילה early, which fits the ruling in step 13.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי davened the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת beside a certain pillar.

steps.title: עולא's different version of the story
steps.stepSummary: עולא reports that the story happened beside a palm tree, not a pillar. The person was רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, and he davened the מוצאי שבת תפילה on שבת, not the שבת תפילה on ערב שבת.
steps.simpleTranslation: When עולא came, he said: It was beside a palm tree, not beside a pillar. It was not רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי but רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי. And it was not the שבת prayer on Friday, but the מוצאי שבת prayer davened on שבת.
steps.whatsHappening: עולא arrives with a different version of the same story and corrects three details: the place, the person, and which תפילה was davened.
steps.deeperAnalysis: עולא changes every detail of the story in step 16. In his version, the story is not an example of davening שבת early at all. It is an example of davening מוצאי שבת early, which matches רבי יאשיה's practice from step 11.

keyTerms.meaning: When עולא came (from ארץ ישראל to בבל)

steps.whatToRemember: There are two versions of the story. In עולא's version it was רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, beside a palm tree, davening מוצאי שבת on שבת.
steps.confusionAlert: עולא is not arguing about the הלכה. He is correcting the details of a story. Both early practices, on Friday and on שבת afternoon, were already allowed by שמואל in steps 13 and 15.

phrases.english: When Ulla came, he said:
It was beside a palm tree,
and it was not beside a pillar.

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: And it was not Rabbi Yishmael, son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בְּרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הֲוָה,
phrases.english: but rather it was Rabbi Elazar, son of Rabbi Yosei,

phrases.aramaic: וְלֹא שֶׁל שַׁבָּת בְּעֶרֶב שַׁבָּת הֲוָה,
phrases.english: and it was not the Shabbat prayer on the eve of Shabbat,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא שֶׁל מוֹצָאֵי שַׁבָּת בְּשַׁבָּת הֲוָה.
phrases.english: but rather it was the prayer of the conclusion of Shabbat on Shabbat.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a competing tradition that changes the place, the person, and the תפילה in the story of step 16.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the factual details of the pillar story as reported in step 16.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: In עולא's version, the place was a palm tree, the person was רבי אלעזר ברבי יוסי, and the תפילה was the מוצאי שבת תפילה davened on שבת.

steps.title: What does 'no fixed time' mean for the evening prayer?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about תפלת הערב and asks what 'אין לה קבע' means.
steps.simpleTranslation: The evening prayer has no fixed time. What does 'has no fixed time' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a phrase from the משנה and asks what it really means. This sets up the next few steps.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The phrase 'אין לה קבע' could mean two different things: no fixed hour, or no fixed obligation. The גמרא wants to figure out which one the משנה means.

keyTerms.meaning: It has no fixed setting (time or obligation)

phrases.english: The evening prayer has no fixed time.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה, which the גמרא now comes back to explain.

phrases.english: What does 'has no fixed time' mean?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the stories about davening early on ערב שבת and מוצאי שבת and starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The meaning of the משנה's phrase 'אין לה קבע' about עַרְבִית.

steps.title: It can't just mean 'any time at night'
steps.stepSummary: If it only meant you can daven any time during the night, the משנה should have said 'all night.'
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say it means that if he wants, he may daven the whole night, then the משנה should have said 'the evening prayer may be said all night'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries one possible meaning, that you can daven עַרְבִית any time at night, and rejects it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the משנה meant 'any time at night,' clearer words were available: 'כל הלילה.' Since the משנה chose the odd wording 'אין לה קבע,' it must mean something else.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (a suggested reading that will be rejected)
Let it teach / it should have said

steps.confusionAlert: Don't walk away thinking עַרְבִית has a fixed hour. The גמרא is only saying that this is not what 'אין לה קבע' means here.

phrases.english: If you say that if he wants
he may daven the whole night,
then let it teach: 'The evening prayer, all night'!

steps.triggerLanguage: אִילֵּימָא דְּאִי בָּעֵי מְצַלֵּי כּוּלֵּיהּ לֵילְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tries a first answer to the question in Step 18 and rejects it.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that 'אין לה קבע' means you can daven any time at night.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If that were the meaning, the משנה would have used the clearer wording 'כל הלילה.'

steps.title: It means עַרְבִית is optional
steps.stepSummary: 'No fixed' means the משנה follows the view that עַרְבִית is רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, what does 'has no fixed' mean? It follows the one who said the evening prayer is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its real answer: 'אין לה קבע' means עַרְבִית is not a fixed obligation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'קבע' now means 'fixed duty' instead of 'fixed time.' So the משנה is taking a side in a known argument: עַרְבִית is רשות.

phrases.english: Rather, what does 'has no fixed' mean?
It follows the one who said
the evening prayer is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After Step 19 rejected the first reading, this gives the correct one.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'אין לה קבע' means עַרְבִית is רשות, following the view that it is optional.

steps.title: The source: רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע argue
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה quotes שמואל: רבן גמליאל says עַרְבִית is חובה, רבי יהושע says it is רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: For רב יהודה said that שמואל said: About the evening prayer, רבן גמליאל says it is required, and רבי יהושע says it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows where the 'optional' view comes from. It is a מחלוקת between two great תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 20 said the משנה follows 'the one who said רשות.' Here we learn who that is: רבי יהושע. So the משנה's wording matches רבי יהושע against רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: The נשיא (head of the Sages), who holds עַרְבִית is required
תנא who holds עַרְבִית is optional

phrases.english: For רב יהודה said that שמואל said:
The evening prayer:
רבן גמליאל says it is required,
רבי יהושע says it is optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Backs up Step 20 by naming the source of the 'רשות' view.
steps.raayaObject: That there is a known view that עַרְבִית is רשות, which the משנה follows.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The statement of רב יהודה in the name of שמואל reporting the מחלוקת of רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.

steps.title: אביי and רבא argue over the הלכה
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules like the view that עַרְבִית is חובה; רבא rules like the view that it is רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: The הלכה follows the one who says it is required. And רבא said: The הלכה follows the one who says it is optional.
steps.whatsHappening: Two later אמוראים give opposite rulings on the argument between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument does not end with the תנאים. אביי sides with רבן גמליאל (חובה), and רבא sides with רבי יהושע (רשות).

keyTerms.meaning: Following the words of the one who says
Two leading אמוראים who often argue

steps.whatToRemember: The משנה's 'אין לה קבע' means עַרְבִית is רשות, like רבי יהושע. רבן גמליאל says חובה. אביי rules חובה, and רבא rules רשות.

phrases.english: אביי said:
The הלכה follows the one who says it is required.
And רבא said:
The הלכה follows the one who says it is optional.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי הֲלָכָה כְּדִבְרֵי הָאוֹמֵר חוֹבָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the מחלוקת in Step 21, this gives the opposing rulings on it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אביי: the הלכה is that עַרְבִית is חובה. רבא: the הלכה is that עַרְבִית is רשות.

steps.title: A student asks רבי יהושע and hears 'optional'
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא tells of a student who asked רבי יהושע whether עַרְבִית is required, and he answered רשות.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: There was a story of a student who came before רבי יהושע. He asked: Is the evening prayer optional or required? He answered: Optional.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a famous story from a ברייתא about the same question. This is the first part of the story.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע answers exactly as he held in Step 21: רשות. The story is set up so the student will next ask רבן גמליאל.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
There was a story with one student
who came before רבי יהושע.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת אוֹ חוֹבָה?
phrases.english: He said to him: Is the evening prayer optional or required?
He said to him: Optional.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a story that shows the מחלוקת from Step 21 in real life.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע tells the student that עַרְבִית is רשות.

steps.title: The student asks רבן גמליאל and hears 'required'
steps.stepSummary: The same student asks רבן גמליאל, who answers חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came before רבן גמליאל and asked: Is the evening prayer optional or required? He answered: Required.
steps.whatsHappening: The student asks the same question to רבן גמליאל and gets the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the student holds two opposite answers from two great רבנים. This sets up the clash in the next step.

phrases.english: He came before רבן גמליאל,

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לוֹ: תְּפִלַּת עַרְבִית רְשׁוּת אוֹ חוֹבָה?
phrases.english: he said to him: Is the evening prayer optional or required?
He said to him: Required.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from Step 23, now with רבן גמליאל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל tells the student that עַרְבִית is חובה.

steps.title: The student points out the clash
steps.stepSummary: The student challenges רבן גמליאל: didn't רבי יהושע tell me it is רשות?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But didn't רבי יהושע tell me it is optional?!
steps.whatsHappening: The student tells רבן גמליאל that רבי יהושע gave him the opposite answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real challenge to רבן גמליאל's ruling, because another great Sage disagrees. The student wants to know which answer to follow.

phrases.english: He said to him: But didn't רבי יהושע
tell me it is optional?!

steps.triggerLanguage: וַהֲלֹא רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ אָמַר לִי רְשׁוּת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the two answers from Steps 23 and 24 against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבן גמליאל's ruling that עַרְבִית is חובה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יהושע, another great Sage, ruled that it is רשות.

steps.title: Wait until the scholars gather in the בית המדרש
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells the student to wait until the scholars enter the בית המדרש, where the matter will be raised.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wait until the shield-bearers come into the בית המדרש.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל does not answer right away. He says the question will be brought up publicly when all the scholars are together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Instead of arguing with the student in private, רבן גמליאל plans to raise it in front of the whole בית המדרש. This sets up the next part of the story.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wait
until the shield-bearers come in
phrases.notes: He means the Torah scholars, who 'battle' over Torah like soldiers with shields.

phrases.english: to the study hall.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמְתֵּן עַד שֶׁיִּכָּנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין לְבֵית הַמִּדְרָשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: רבן גמליאל responds to the student's challenge in Step 25.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question will be settled publicly in the בית המדרש once the scholars arrive.

steps.title: The question is asked in front of all the scholars
steps.stepSummary: Once the great scholars come into the בית המדרש, the student asks whether עַרְבִית is רשות or חובה, and רבן גמליאל answers חובה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When the great scholars came in, the student stood up and asked: Is the evening prayer optional or required? רבן גמליאל answered: Required.
steps.whatsHappening: The plan from step 26 is carried out. The question is now asked publicly, and רבן גמליאל gives his ruling in front of everyone.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Before this, the question was asked in private. Now רבן גמליאל's answer of חובה is a public ruling. This sets up the clash with רבי יהושע's private answer of רשות.

keyTerms.meaning: Masters of the shields, a nickname for the leading Torah scholars

phrases.english: When the masters of the shields entered,
phrases.notes: This is a nickname for the leading scholars, the ones רבן גמליאל said to wait for in step 26.

phrases.english: the questioner stood and asked:
Is the evening prayer optional or obligatory?
Rabban Gamliel said to him: Obligatory.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁנִּכְנְסוּ בַּעֲלֵי תְּרִיסִין, עָמַד הַשּׁוֹאֵל וְשָׁאַל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Carries out רבן גמליאל's instruction to wait for the scholars.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבן גמליאל publicly rules that עַרְבִית is חובה.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל asks if anyone disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל asks the scholars whether anyone disputes his ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to the Sages: Is there anyone who disagrees about this?
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל asks the room whether anyone disagrees. This sets up a response from רבי יהושע.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He already knows רבי יהושע was quoted as saying רשות. The question gives רבי יהושע a chance to state his opinion openly in front of everyone.

keyTerms.meaning: Is there any, used to open a question

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said to the Sages:

phrases.aramaic: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁחוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה?
phrases.english: Is there any person who disputes this matter?

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּלוּם יֵשׁ אָדָם שֶׁחוֹלֵק בְּדָבָר זֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows the public ruling with a check for disagreement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether any scholar disputes that עַרְבִית is חובה.

steps.title: רבי יהושע says no one disagrees
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע answers that no one disputes the ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע said to him: No.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע answers that no one disagrees, even though he himself had told the student רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהושע chooses not to argue publicly with the נשיא. This sets him up for the challenge that comes next.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua said to him: No.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבן גמליאל's question.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל confronts רבי יהושע
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל challenges רבי יהושע: wasn't רשות said in your name?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said to him: But they told me in your name that it is optional!
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל points out that רבי יהושע's 'no' does not match what he told the student.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The private ruling of רשות from step 23 is now brought out in public. רבי יהושע has to explain the contradiction.

keyTerms.meaning: But is it not so that...

phrases.english: He said to him:
phrases.notes: This is רבן גמליאל speaking to רבי יהושע.

phrases.english: But was it not in your name that they told me "optional"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks רבי יהושע's answer in step 29.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהושע's claim that no one disagrees.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He himself was quoted as ruling רשות, so he does disagree.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל orders רבי יהושע to stand
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל tells רבי יהושע to stand so that witnesses can testify against him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: יהושע, stand up, and they will testify against you.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל treats the moment like a court case and makes רבי יהושע stand up. This sets up רבי יהושע's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Standing while being testified against is how a person is treated in court. The confrontation turns personal and public.

keyTerms.meaning: And they will testify against you

phrases.english: He said to him: Yehoshua,
stand on your feet and they will testify against you.

steps.triggerLanguage: יְהוֹשֻׁעַ, עֲמוֹד עַל רַגְלֶיךָ וְיָעִידוּ בְּךָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Raises the pressure of the challenge.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי יהושע must stand and face the testimony.

steps.title: רבי יהושע admits he said it
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע admits he cannot deny saying רשות, since the student is alive and present.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהושע stood up and said: If I were alive and he were dead, the living could deny what the dead person said. But now that we are both alive, how can one living person deny another?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יהושע stands and admits that he did tell the student רשות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He explains that he cannot deny it while the student is standing right there. So he admits what he said.

keyTerms.meaning: If it were the case that

phrases.aramaic: עָמַד רַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עַל רַגְלָיו וְאָמַר
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehoshua stood on his feet and said:
If I were alive and he were dead,
phrases.notes: "He" is the student who asked the question.

phrases.english: the living could contradict the dead.
But now that I am alive and he is alive,

phrases.aramaic: הֵיאַךְ יָכוֹל הַחַי לְהַכְחִישׁ אֶת הַחַי?
phrases.english: how can the living contradict the living?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge by admitting it.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes, I said רשות, and I cannot deny it while the student is alive and present.

steps.title: The crowd stops רבן גמליאל's lecture
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל keeps lecturing while רבי יהושע stays standing, until the upset crowd tells the interpreter to stop.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל sat and taught while רבי יהושע stood, until all the people grumbled and told חוצפית the interpreter: Stop! And he stopped.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל keeps רבי יהושע standing as he teaches. The people get upset and shut down the lecture.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument about עַרְבִית has turned into a matter of how the נשיא treats a great scholar. When the interpreter stops, the lecture cannot reach the crowd.

keyTerms.meaning: Interpreter who repeated the teacher's words aloud to the crowd

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel was sitting and lecturing,
and Rabbi Yehoshua was standing on his feet,
until all the people murmured
and said to Chutzpit the interpreter:
Stop! And he stopped.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָיָה רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל יוֹשֵׁב וְדוֹרֵשׁ וְרַבִּי יְהוֹשֻׁעַ עוֹמֵד עַל רַגְלָיו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes what happened after רבי יהושע admitted it.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The people halt the lecture in protest.

steps.title: The people decide to remove רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The people list three times רבן גמליאל humiliated רבי יהושע and decide to remove him as נשיא.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said: How long will he keep hurting him? Last ראש השנה he hurt him. In the case of firstborn animals, in the story of רבי צדוק, he hurt him. Here too he hurt him. Come, let's remove him!
steps.whatsHappening: The people decide that this is one time too many and say רבן גמליאל should be removed from being נשיא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: They point to a pattern. This is the third time רבי יהושע was publicly hurt, after ראש השנה and the בכורות case. That pattern is their reason to remove him.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us remove him from office

steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether עַרְבִית is רשות or חובה led to רבי יהושע being humiliated in public, and that led the people to remove רבן גמליאל as נשיא.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the famous story of how רבן גמליאל was removed from being נשיא, which the גמרא goes on to tell.

phrases.english: They said: How long will he go on afflicting him?
On Rosh Hashana last year he afflicted him.
phrases.notes: This is the famous story in מסכת ראש השנה about which day was יום כיפור.

phrases.english: Regarding firstborn animals, in the incident of Rabbi Tzadok, he afflicted him.
Here too he afflicted him.
Come, let us remove him!
phrases.notes: They mean removing רבן גמליאל from being נשיא.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the crowd's protest and turns it into a decision.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because this is the third time, רבן גמליאל should be removed as נשיא.

steps.title: Who should replace רבן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The people ask whom they should appoint in place of רבן גמליאל.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whom shall we appoint?
steps.whatsHappening: The decision to remove רבן גמליאל has been made, so now the people ask who should take his place. This question sets up the next few steps, where candidates are suggested and judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Removing a leader leaves a gap that must be filled. The question opens a short selection process. Each candidate will be checked against what could go wrong with רבן גמליאל still around.

keyTerms.meaning: we will appoint (literally: we will set up / make stand)

phrases.english: Whom shall we appoint (in his place)?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Follows directly from the decision in step 34 to remove רבן גמליאל.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which חכם should become the new נשיא.

steps.title: רבי יהושע is ruled out
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהושע is suggested, but he is rejected because he was the one involved in the incident.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we appoint רבי יהושע? No, he is a party to the incident.
steps.whatsHappening: The first candidate, רבי יהושע, is suggested and immediately rejected. He was the person רבן גמליאל humiliated, so he is too personally involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fight was between רבן גמליאל and רבי יהושע. Putting רבי יהושע in his place would look like the winner taking the prize. That would deeply hurt רבן גמליאל.

keyTerms.meaning: a party to the incident, the person directly involved

phrases.english: Shall we appoint Rabbi Yehoshua?
He is a party to the incident.
phrases.notes: He's the one רבן גמליאל embarrassed, so giving him the job would really sting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects the first answer to the question in step 35.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי יהושע as a candidate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He was personally involved in the conflict with רבן גמליאל.

steps.title: רבי עקיבא is ruled out
steps.stepSummary: רבי עקיבא is suggested, but rejected because he has no ancestral merit to protect him from punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we appoint רבי עקיבא? Perhaps he will be punished, because he has no merit of ancestors.
steps.whatsHappening: The second candidate, רבי עקיבא, is suggested and rejected. The worry is that he could be punished because he lacks זכות אבות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל might resent whoever replaces him. Someone with great ancestors is protected by their merit, but רבי עקיבא does not have that protection. So he would be vulnerable.

keyTerms.meaning: the merit of one's ancestors, which protects a person

steps.confusionAlert: This does not say רבי עקיבא was not great enough. He is turned down only because he lacks protection from his family line.

phrases.english: Shall we appoint Rabbi Akiva?
Perhaps he will cause him to be punished,
phrases.notes: The "he" who might cause punishment is רבן גמליאל, and the one punished is רבי עקיבא.

phrases.english: since he does not have the merit of ancestors.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers and rejects a second answer to step 35.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי עקיבא as a candidate.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He lacks זכות אבות and could be punished.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is chosen
steps.stepSummary: They decide on רבי אלעזר בן עזריה because he is wise, rich, and a tenth-generation descendant of עזרא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, let us appoint רבי אלעזר בן עזריה, since he is wise, he is rich, and he is the tenth generation from עזרא.
steps.whatsHappening: After two rejections, the people pick רבי אלעזר בן עזריה. They list three qualities that make him right for the job.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word אלא shows a turn away from the rejected options to the real answer. His three qualities are listed here. The next step explains why each one matters.

keyTerms.meaning: the tenth generation descendant of עזרא

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה,
phrases.english: Rather, let us appoint Rabbi Elazar ben Azarya,
for he is wise, and he is rich,
and he is the tenth generation from Ezra.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא נוֹקְמֵיהּ לְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר בֶּן עֲזַרְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the accepted answer after rejecting two candidates.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה should be appointed.

steps.title: Why each of his three qualities matters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains each quality: wisdom to answer challenges, wealth to represent the Jews at the Roman court, and ancestry to protect him from punishment.
steps.simpleTranslation: He is wise, so if he is challenged, he can answer. He is rich, so if someone must go pay respects at the קיסר's court, he too can go. He is the tenth from עזרא, so he has זכות אבות and cannot be punished.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes through the three qualities one by one and explains what each protects against.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each quality answers a real problem. Wisdom means רבן גמליאל cannot embarrass him with hard questions. Wealth lets him represent the community before the government. His ancestry gives him the protection רבי עקיבא lacked.
steps.whatToRemember: Each of רבי אלעזר בן עזריה's qualities solves a specific problem: wisdom handles challenges, wealth handles the government, and ancestry handles protection.

phrases.english: "He is wise":
so if he is challenged, he will answer it.
"And he is rich":

phrases.aramaic: דְּאִי אִית לֵיהּ לְפַלּוֹחֵי לְבֵי קֵיסָר,
phrases.english: so if there is a need to pay homage at the emperor's court,
he too can go and pay homage.
"And he is the tenth from Ezra":
so he has the merit of ancestors,
and he cannot cause him to be punished.

steps.triggerLanguage: הוּא חָכָם דְּאִי מַקְשֵׁי לֵיהּ מְפָרֵק לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the three qualities listed in step 38. The third quality directly answers the problem raised about רבי עקיבא in step 37.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Each quality protects the new leader: wisdom against challenges, wealth for dealing with the government, and ancestry against punishment.

steps.title: The offer and consulting his wife
steps.stepSummary: They offer him the position. He says he will consult his household, and he goes to ask his wife.
steps.simpleTranslation: They came and said to him: Would the Master agree to be head of the ישיבה? He said to them: I will go and consult with my household. He went and consulted with his wife. She said to him:
steps.whatsHappening: The people offer רבי אלעזר בן עזריה the job, and he goes to ask his wife first. The step ends with "She said to him," which sets up her answer in the next part.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story moves from choosing a candidate to actually asking him. Instead of accepting right away, he asks his household. His wife's response comes next.

phrases.english: They came and said to him:
Would the Master agree
to be head of the academy?
He said to them:
I will go and consult with the people of my household.
He went and consulted with his wife.
She said to him:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After choosing him in steps 38 and 39, the people now go to make the actual offer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי אלעזר בן עזריה is offered the leadership and consults his wife before answering.
